description: Polonium is a rare and highly radioactive metal with no stable isotopes, classified as a chalcogen chemically similar to selenium and tellurium, though its metallic character resembles thallium, lead, and bismuth. It has symbol Po and atomic number 84, with all 42 known isotopes being radioactive. Due to the short half-life of all its isotopes, its natural occurrence is limited to tiny traces, primarily polonium-210 in uranium ores.
uses: Polonium has few applications, all related to its radioactivity: heaters in space probes, antistatic devices, sources of neutrons and alpha particles, and as a poison. It was also used as a key ingredient in the 'Urchin' initiator at the center of nuclear bomb pits during the Manhattan Project.
characteristics: Polonium exists in two metallic allotropes, with the alpha form being a simple cubic crystal structure at standard temperature and pressure. Polonium-210 is an alpha emitter with a half-life of 138.4 days and is 5,000 times more radioactive than radium; it becomes airborne with ease, with 50% vaporization occurring at 55°C in 45 hours, despite having a melting point of 254°C and boiling point of 962°C. Polonium dissolves readily in dilute acids and its solutions change from pink to yellow due to alpha radiation ionizing the solvent and converting Po2+ into Po4+.
